## labs/nvidia/luxdit

LuxDiT - Estimates image-based lighting from a single photo or video with a video diffusion transformer.

Status: blocked-license. Install: none. Artifact: source-build. Arm64: unknown. GB10: unverified. Comfy shape: none.
Input: one image or a video
Output: an environment light estimate for relighting
Licenses: code NVIDIA OneWay Noncommercial License. Weights Hugging Face card tagged license:other. Commercial use non-commercial.
Footprint: 24 GB VRAM, 40 GB disk. Weights: nvidia/LuxDiT/luxdit_image/@11.74.
Artifact ref: https://github.com/nv-tlabs/LuxDiT.git
Upstream: https://github.com/nv-tlabs/LuxDiT
Also: https://huggingface.co/nvidia/LuxDiT
Sources: https://github.com/nv-tlabs/LuxDiT

Nothing in this graph touches the GPU. The row's work runs outside the Comfy process through the operator CLI, so the App claims no occupancy and stops no heavy job: the one-heavy-job rule is the CLI's to enforce, next to the heavy confirm and the headroom preflight.

Operator verbs (host shell):
  bazelisk run //:manage -- nvidia-lab status
  bazelisk run //:manage -- nvidia-lab plan luxdit

Canvas:
1. Preflight prints whether this Spark could run the row today - the catalog row, an aarch64 host, the binary that row's install kind needs, and the artifact ref.
2. The verdict card prints the blocking reason and the sentence that would reopen the row.
3. The tier table prints all 18 rows with their status and licenses.

Gate notes: The repository ships the NVIDIA OneWay Noncommercial License, so the code itself, not only the weights, bars use in a product container. This is the relighting capability the 3D lane does not have, which is why the card is worth keeping.
Reopen: NVIDIA relicense the code away from the OneWay Noncommercial terms.
Verify: bazelisk test //tests:bats_nvidia_lab_test

Occupancy: none - stop nothing GPU. One GB10 job.
